key_insight: Fourier-circuit configuration affects both LiDAR classification accuracy and noise sensitivity: IQFT-After performs best on ideal KITTI simulations, while No-QFT and Trainable-QFT are more robust under noise.
engineering_relevance: Hardware-aware circuit selection can balance predictive performance, quantum resource requirements, and noise robustness in hybrid point-cloud classifiers.
method: Combine PointNet feature extraction, amplitude encoding, and a variational quantum circuit.
Compare No-QFT, Full-QFT-After, QFT-no-swap, IQFT-After, and Trainable-QFT.
Remove final QFT SWAP gates to reduce complexity while preserving Pauli-Z features up to a fixed permutation.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on KITTI, nuScenes, and PandaSet across three seeds includes IBM FakeManilaV2 noise simulations; ideal KITTI weighted F1 is 0.857 ± 0.033 for IQFT-After versus 0.838 ± 0.023 for No-QFT.
watch_item: Noise-model simulations do not establish real-hardware performance, and the best ideal-simulation circuit may not remain best under noise.
paper_title: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification
